citations.S1: SQL injection (critical)** — `"... = '%s'" % (user_id, status)`. Attacker-controlled request params go straight into SQL.
citations.S2: Connection/cursor never closed (medium)** — no `close()`, no `try/finally`, no context manager. Under load this leaks SQLite connections/file handles.
citations.S3: TypeError in `format_receipt` (high)** — `order[0]` (an `id`, an int) is concatenated with `+` to a string
citations.S4: Division by zero in `average_order_value` (high)** — a user with zero matching orders crashes the request
citations.S5: Money stored/summed as float (high for e-commerce)** ... Binary floats can't represent cents exactly
citations.S6: `apply_discount` doesn't validate `pct` (medium)** — negative or >100 values silently produce negative or nonsensical prices.
citations.S7: No input validation on `status` (medium)** ... Fix: validate against a known set of statuses (enum/allow-list)
citations.S8: Missing authorization / IDOR risk (critical...)** — nothing here confirms `user_id` is the authenticated caller's own ID.
citations.S11: a locked/corrupt DB or bad path raises a raw `sqlite3` exception up through the HTTP handler, potentially leaking internals in an error response
citations.S13: Unbounded query / no pagination (medium)** — `fetchall()` with no `LIMIT`
citations.S14: Result rows are unnamed tuples (low)** — `order[0]`, `o[1]` etc. are fragile to any column reorder
